distribution.title: Normal distribution
distribution.intro: The normal distribution is a continuous, symmetric distribution described by its mean \(\mu\) and standard deviation \(\sigma>0\). The standard normal has \(\mu=0\) and \(\sigma=1\).
distribution.properties: Its mean is \(\mu\) and variance is \(\sigma^2\). If \(X\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)\), then \((X-\mu)/\sigma\sim N(0,1)\). A multivariate normal generalizes this to vectors with a mean vector and covariance matrix.
distribution.cdf_caption: At each x, the cumulative curve gives the area under the density curve to the left of x.
distribution.course: The course uses normal samples in maximum likelihood estimation and normal, t, and chi-squared distributions to construct confidence intervals.
distribution.course_link: Use the normal model to estimate a mean
distribution.r_intro: These examples use functions from R’s stats package. For functions with d, p, q, and r prefixes, they compute a density or mass, cumulative probability, quantile, and random samples, respectively.
distribution.r_code:
dnorm(0, mean = 0, sd = 1)
pnorm(1.96)
qnorm(0.975)
rnorm(100, mean = 0, sd = 1)
